items.title: [MacRumors] Next iPad Air Likely to Have These 10 New Features
items.content_html:
Earlier today, it was once again reported that the next-generation iPad Air will be equipped with an OLED display, albeit with a 60Hz refresh rate. That is not all, of course, with the new iPad mini announced last month likely providing us with a preview of some other upgrades coming to the iPad Air in the first half of 2027.


Below, we have outlined 10 new features that are likely for the next iPad Air:
  • OLED display with more vivid colors and increased contrast ratio, but likely 60Hz still

  • Thinner bezels around the display

  • Nano-texture display option for reduced glare

  • M5 chip: up to 20% faster performance compared to the M4 chip in the current model

  • Approximately 15% thinner and 15% lighter design compared to the current model

  • Acoustic Display: screen vibrations produce sound, no speaker holes

  • IP67-rated water and dust resistance

  • Apple's C2 modem in cellular models with "meaningfully faster uploads" compared to Apple's previous C1X modem

  • Adaptive True Tone flash for improved photos and document scanning

  • Fast-charging support: up to 50% in 30 minutes with a 35W or higher adapter
A specific timeframe for the next iPad Air has yet to be rumored, but an announcement in March or April next year is a reasonable guess.

items.title: [agbz.ru] Russia lets small farms use grants to repay up to 20% of loans
items.content_html: Russia has changed its agricultural support program to let small businesses use grants to repay up to 20% of loans for farm development, agricultural consumer cooperatives, rural bakeries and agricultural projects by participants in the special military operation. The government also dropped a documentation requirement for subsidized equipment purchases costing up to 3 million rubles: recipients no longer need to prove the equipment is listed in the Russian industrial-products register or the register for industrial products with no Russian analogues. Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin signed the changes. Grants for dairy-farm acceleration projects launched this year will continue in 2027. The 2027 federal budget allocates more than 6.5 billion rubles to support small agribusinesses.

items.title: [agritechinsights.com] Farmers and researchers urge tailored approaches to climate-resilient agriculture
items.content_html: Agricultural researchers, farmers and development groups are backing locally tailored approaches to climate resilience, from regenerative practices and organic farming to irrigation investment and farmer cooperatives. A study of agriculture’s early spread finds that knowledge diffusion influenced its expansion more than climate variables did, while a separate carbon-farming model suggests smallholders may need to pool resources to make participation financially feasible. In western Kansas, The Nature Conservancy and General Mills argue that regenerative programs should address landscape-specific problems such as Ogallala Aquifer depletion, rather than measure success by enrolled acreage alone. Oklahoma farmer Matt Moreland and Rabobank grains strategist Stephen Nicholson point to lower input costs and eventual yield gains from soil-health practices, while warning that farmers need to manage transition costs and financing. Other approaches include the Republika Srpska government’s plans to expand irrigation and encourage drought-resistant crops, and organic agriculture programs in 15 Asian and African countries described by Korea Hope Foundation chair Seo Buk-won.

items.title: [dagenslantbruk.se] Swedish 2025 field-trial report details crop management strategies
items.content_html: Swedish agricultural organization Hushållningssällskapet has published its Sverigeförsöken 2025 report, compiling hundreds of independent field trials on crop nutrition, irrigation, tillage, crop protection and variety testing. The trials covered growing conditions from Skåne in the south to northern Sweden, with findings intended to help farmers weigh yield and resource use under changing conditions. The report says irrigation strategies for spring barley can stabilize yields and quality in dry years, while findings on crop varieties and crop protection can guide treatment choices and timing. Hushållningssällskapet says it uses the results in farm advice, field visits and decision-support tools; the full report is available online at sverigeforsoken.se.

items.title: [agronews.com.pl] Farmers in Poland and Serbia face subsidy deadlines and delays
items.content_html: Polish farmers enrolled in a carbon-farming scheme must submit proof of specified manure and slurry practices to the government’s payments agency by Nov. 9, 2026, or risk problems with their payments. Farms in listed municipalities where wet weather prevented fieldwork may qualify for an extension to Nov. 30. In Serbia, farmers are still waiting for the second installment of crop-production subsidies; caretaker Agriculture Minister Dragan Glamočić said decisions should be left to the next government. Separately, the Łódź regional agricultural chamber is seeking an additional application round for soil-liming grants after the Oct. 15 deadline, citing harvest workloads, delivery delays and slow soil-test results. The regional fund had allocated 2.5 million złoty, with grants capped at 20,000 zł per farm.

items.title: [dagenslantbruk.se] Farmers urged to tailor grazing to grassland recovery and climate
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Agricultural specialists in Sweden, France and South Africa say grassland management requires continued upkeep and grazing adapted to local vegetation and weather. Sweden’s inventory found that the natural and cultural values of most re-surveyed meadows and pastures remained broadly stable, while French livestock farmers discussed how the 2026 drought and heat affected forage production. University of Limpopo pasture scientist Lesego Motshekga says rotational grazing works only when stocking rates match available forage and plants have time to recover; moving animals between camps alone cannot prevent overgrazing. Motshekga recommends deciding when to move livestock based on grass condition rather than a fixed calendar.

items.title: 🔓 [Fast Company] 3.6 million ladders sold at Lowe’s, Costco, and Amazon are being recalled after fall-related brain injuries, broken bones reported
items.content_html:
Millions of Americans will begin putting up Christmas lights and trees in the weeks ahead, and many will rely on ladders to hang the decorations just right.

But now the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has issued an alert notifying consumers that 3.6 million ladders are being recalled because they could unexpectedly retract.

And unfortunately, numerous people have already sustained broken bones, brain damage, and other injuries as a result. Here’s what you need to know.

What’s happened?

On November 5, the CPSC published a recall notice alerting consumers that approximately 3,662,000 ladders made by Little Giant Ladder Systems were being recalled after the company received several reports of the ladders unexpectedly retracting, causing serious injuries to users.

The CPSC is warning that “The ladders can suddenly retract if the Rapid Locks are not fully engaged, posing a fall hazard to consumers.”

It explains that the Rapid Locks are black or orange components on the ladders’ legs, designed to be inserted to adjust the ladders’ height. When the Rapid Locks don’t work as intended, the ladders can suddenly retract, causing the user to fall and sustain serious injuries.

Little Giant has also published its own recall notice, in which the ladder manufacturer warns of the same hazard.

Have people been injured?

Unfortunately, yes. And the injuries are serious.

According to the CPSC notice, Little Giant has received 39 reports of the Rapid Locks not working properly on its ladders. It has also received 25 reports of the ladders retracting.

Further, the company has received 19 reports of people being injured. The most serious are three reports of head injuries, which include:

  • traumatic brain injury
  • skull fracture
  • concussion
  • vision loss
  • hearing loss
  • cognitive impairment

The 16 other injuries reported include:

  • joint or bone fracture
  • lacerations
  • bruising

Which ladders are being recalled?

The CPSC says the following models of Little Giant ladders are being recalled:

  • Adjustable Fortress 2.0
  • Conquest 2.0
  • Dark Horse 2.0
  • Epic
  • King Kombo XT
  • Leveler
  • MegaLite
  • MegaLite+
  • Multi
  • Quantum
  • Vector

“The brand name Little Giant and the model name are located on the side of the ladder,” the notice notes. “Only ladders without an orange rectangular ‘QC’ sticker on the rail above one of the Rapid Locks are included in this recall.”

Little Giant’s recall notice lists the specific part numbers of the various ladder models being recalled, which you can find here.

Where were the recalled ladders sold?

The more than 3.6 million ladders included in this recall were sold nationally between December 2015 and October 2026. The ladders sold for anywhere from around $100 to around $1,000.

The affected ladders were sold in the following stores:

  • Lowe’s
  • Costco
  • other stores nationwide

They were also sold online at:

  • Lowes.com
  • Amazon.com
  • Costco.com
  • LittleGiantLadders.com
  • other websites

What to do if you have a recalled ladder

The CPSC says that consumers should stop using the affected ladders immediately until they review the Little Giant ladders recall page, or the information provided by scanning the QR code on the ladders, and contact Little Giant for a repair kit.

That repair kit contains “additional instructions and labels, which should be affixed to the ladder,” the CPSC notice states. The additional instructions “advise consumers to verify that their Rapid Locks are properly engaged before every use and to maintain their locks with lubrication.”

If the ladder does not function properly after that, consumers should contact Little Giant for an evaluation. If the ladder fails to act as intended, Little Giant will then replace it with an equivalent model or offer a refund. 

Owners of ladders included in the recall are urged to read both recall notices for full instructions and contact Little Giant with any questions.

A spokesperson for Little Giant Ladder Services emailed the following statement:

“We recently identified a very small number of instances out of the more than 3.6 million Rapid Lock ladders sold since 2015 in which the locks had not been properly engaged before use. Out of an abundance of caution, we initiated a voluntary recall of the affected ladders in coordination with the CPSC. Through this recall, we will be providing at no expense to each customer new warning labels and additional instructional materials to help them verify that the Rapid Locks on their ladder are properly engaged before every use. These additional instructions also urge customers to maintain their Rapid Locks with proper lubrication.”
